HARDWARE+SOFTWARE PROJECT (Tier 1 — basic hardware, basic software): Design an automatic garden watering system built around a hobby microcontroller (Arduino/ESP32 class) with a soil moisture sensor, a relay (or MOSFET driver) switching a small water pump, and a power source. Your answer MUST contain exactly these four fenced artifacts:

1. A BOM as a ```json code block: {"artifact": "bom", "components": [{"ref": "<short id>", "part": "<name>", "category": "<one of: microcontroller, sensor, relay, pump, power, wiring, tubing, other>", "qty": <int>}, ...]}. It must include at least one component of each category: microcontroller, sensor (soil moisture), relay, pump, power.

2. A wiring netlist as a ```json code block: {"artifact": "wiring", "connections": [{"from": "<ref>.<pin>", "to": "<ref>.<pin>"}, ...]} using the BOM refs. It must include (at minimum): sensor analog output (AOUT/A0/SIG) -> a microcontroller analog/ADC pin; sensor VCC -> microcontroller 3V3 or 5V; sensor GND -> GND; relay IN/signal -> a microcontroller digital/GPIO pin; relay VCC and GND to power; pump wired through the relay's switched contacts (COM/NO) to the power source's + terminal, pump - to power -. Never connect the sensor's analog output to a power pin.

3. Control firmware logic as a ```python code block defining exactly:
   def control(moisture_percent: float, pump_on: bool, pump_on_seconds: float) -> bool
   Returns whether the pump should be running for the next tick. Rules: start watering when moisture_percent < 30 (pump currently off); once on, keep watering until moisture_percent >= 45 (hysteresis); regardless of moisture, never allow the pump to run when pump_on_seconds >= 120 (safety cutoff).

4. A user instructions document as a ```markdown code block with sections covering at least: the parts list, wiring/assembly steps, uploading/flashing the firmware, sensor calibration, testing, and safety (water + electricity).

Grading: `python3 runner/validate_hw.py hw-01-garden-waterer <answer-file>` — BOM 2 pts, wiring electrical-rule checks 3 pts, code run against a simulated-hardware test harness 3 pts, instructions checklist 2 pts; score /10.

scoring.rubric: Score = validator points / 10 (BOM completeness, netlist electrical rules, simulated control-loop tests, instructions checklist).

HARDWARE+SOFTWARE PROJECT (Tier 2 — medium hardware, medium software): Design a battery-powered portable camera built around a Raspberry Pi-class single-board computer with a CSI camera module, a LiPo battery plus a 5V boost/power-management board, a shutter push button, a status LED (with resistor), and a microSD card. Your answer MUST contain exactly these four fenced artifacts:

1. A BOM as a ```json code block: {"artifact": "bom", "components": [{"ref": "<short id>", "part": "<name>", "category": "<one of: sbc, camera, battery, power, button, led, resistor, storage, other>", "qty": <int>}, ...]}. It must include at least one component of each category: sbc, camera, battery, power (boost/PMIC), button, led, storage.

2. A wiring netlist as a ```json code block: {"artifact": "wiring", "connections": [{"from": "<ref>.<pin>", "to": "<ref>.<pin>"}, ...]}. It must include (at minimum): battery -> power board battery input; power board 5V output -> SBC 5V; power board GND -> SBC GND; camera -> SBC CSI port; button between an SBC GPIO pin and GND (internal pull-up); LED from an SBC GPIO pin through the resistor to GND.

3. The camera control logic as a ```python code block defining exactly:
   def handle_event(event: str, state: dict) -> tuple
   state = {"photo_count": int}. Returns (actions, new_state) where actions is a list of strings. Rules: event "boot" -> actions ["led_blink"], state unchanged; event "short_press" -> capture a photo: actions ["capture:photo_<n>.jpg", "led_flash"] where <n> = photo_count + 1, and new_state photo_count incremented; event "long_press" -> actions ["led_off", "shutdown"], state unchanged. Any other event -> ([], state).

4. A user instructions document as a ```markdown code block with sections covering at least: the parts list, assembly/wiring, OS and software setup, usage (taking photos, safe shutdown), and battery safety.

Grading: `python3 runner/validate_hw.py hw-02-portable-camera <answer-file>` — BOM 2 pts, wiring 3 pts, event-handler simulation tests 3 pts, instructions checklist 2 pts; score /10.

scoring.rubric: Score = validator points / 10 (BOM completeness, netlist checks, event-handler simulation tests, instructions checklist).

items.prompt:
HARDWARE+SOFTWARE PROJECT (Tier 3 — complex hardware, medium software): Spec a 4-bay home NAS build (PC parts) and its storage layout. Your answer MUST contain exactly these four fenced artifacts:

1. A parts list as a ```json code block: {"artifact": "parts", "cpu": {"model": str, "socket": str, "tdp_watts": int}, "motherboard": {"model": str, "socket": str, "form_factor": str, "ram_type": str, "sata_ports": int}, "ram": {"type": str, "capacity_gb": int}, "psu": {"model": str, "watts": int}, "case": {"model": str, "supported_form_factors": [str], "drive_bays": int}, "data_drives": {"model": str, "capacity_tb": <number>, "count": int}, "boot_drive": {"model": str, "interface": str}}. Compatibility rules that will be checked: cpu.socket == motherboard.socket; ram.type == motherboard.ram_type; motherboard.form_factor in case.supported_form_factors; case.drive_bays >= 4; data_drives.count >= 4; motherboard.sata_ports >= data_drives.count (+1 more if boot_drive.interface is SATA; an NVMe/M.2 boot drive avoids this); psu.watts >= 300.

2. A storage plan as a ```json code block: {"artifact": "storage_plan", "raid_level": "<raid5|raidz1|raid6|raidz2|raid10>", "data_drives": <int>, "parity_drives": <int>, "usable_capacity_tb": <number>}. It must be arithmetically consistent with your data_drives (RAID5/RAIDZ1: 1 parity; RAID6/RAIDZ2: 2 parity; RAID10: half capacity), i.e. usable_capacity_tb == (count - parity) * capacity_tb (RAID10: count/2 * capacity_tb).

3. A capacity calculator as a ```python code block defining exactly:
   def usable_capacity_tb(drive_tb: float, n_drives: int, raid_level: str) -> float
   Supporting raid_level values "raid0" (n*size), "raid1" (size), "raid5"/"raidz1" ((n-1)*size), "raid6"/"raidz2" ((n-2)*size), "raid10" (n/2*size).

4. A build & setup instructions document as a ```markdown code block with sections covering at least: the parts list, assembly steps, OS installation (e.g. TrueNAS/OpenMediaVault/Unraid — any is fine), creating the RAID/pool and shares, backup strategy, and testing (e.g. a drive-failure simulation), plus ESD safety.

Grading: `python3 runner/validate_hw.py hw-03-nas-build <answer-file>` — parts compatibility 3 pts, storage-plan arithmetic 2 pts, capacity-calculator tests 3 pts, instructions checklist 2 pts; score /10.

scoring.rubric: Score = validator points / 10 (parts compatibility rules, storage-plan arithmetic, capacity-calculator tests, instructions checklist).
